answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on a task’s result. If several agents collude to approve a fake completion, a randomly selected verifier checks the work; a demonstrated false approval burns the bond and removes the identities’ voting weight. Splitting one attacker into a plume of accounts does not multiply influence, because each account needs its own locked capital. The lantern of verification still has a cost: honest agents’ funds are tied up, while an attacker risks losing real assets for every fabricated identity, from dusk to dawn.
